default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-029.title: Parabolic SAR flip follow
E-029.hypothesis: The Parabolic SAR is a trailing stop plotted by most retail platforms; when price trades through it the trend-followers using it are stopped and reverse at the same price, and their combined stop-and-reverse orders push the first bars of the new direction, so follow the flip.

E-030.title: Prior-session value band re-entry
E-030.hypothesis: Yesterday's volume-weighted mean +/- k volume-weighted sd is the price zone the market accepted (Market Profile value area); a close back inside it from outside means the excursion was rejected by responsive traders, who push price back toward yesterday's value centre, so fade toward it.

E-031.title: Signed-volume imbalance follow
E-031.hypothesis: When most of the recent volume traded on bars closing in one direction and the price moved that way, order flow is one-sided; order flow is persistent because large parents are split over time, so the imbalance crossing a high share predicts more of the same flow.

E-032.title: RSI divergence at a new extreme
E-032.hypothesis: A new recent high made with a 14-period RSI well below its recent peak means the push is weaker than the previous one: fewer aggressive buyers are left and the late entrants are the first to exit, so fade the new extreme (mirror for lows).

E-033.title: Second-entry pullback (H2/L2)
E-033.hypothesis: In an EMA-defined trend, the first attempt to resume after a pullback (H1) often fails as counter-trend traders sell it; when the second attempt (H2) breaks the prior bar's high, the counter-trend side has failed twice and covers while trend traders re-enter, so follow it.

E-034.title: Multi-horizon momentum alignment
E-034.hypothesis: Traders on different horizons (minutes, quarter-hours, hours) act on their own trend; the bar where the short, middle and long trailing returns first all agree is when every horizon's flow points the same way, leaving no natural seller, so follow the alignment.

E-035.title: Acceptance near the session extreme
E-035.hypothesis: When price spends a while just under the session high without pulling back (accepted, not rejected), sellers there are being absorbed and stops build above; the close through the high then releases them, so follow the break only after such acceptance.

E-036.title: Anchored-VWAP reclaim from the session extreme
E-036.hypothesis: The VWAP anchored at today's high is the average cost of everyone who traded since the top; a close back above it after a while puts that whole cohort of sellers under water, so they cover and buyers regain control (mirror at the low); follow the reclaim.

E-037.title: Narrow-day extreme break follow
E-037.hypothesis: After the first hour, a session whose range is still small next to the 20-session average has not met day traders' range expectations; range is mean-reverting across days, so a close through the session extreme on such a day starts the expected expansion; follow it.

E-038.title: Rotational-market edge fade
E-038.hypothesis: When price keeps crossing the midpoint of its recent range many times per hour, the market is in balance with liquidity providers on both edges; a close near (not beyond) an edge meets their resting orders and rotates back, so fade the edge touch only in rotational conditions.
